description: Radiationless decay through accessible conical intersections, avoided crossings, or excited-state crossing funnels controls weak emission or AIE turn-on when the crossing pathway is blocked in aggregates, crystals, or constrained environments.
positive_evidence: computed S1/S0 conical intersection or avoided crossing for the target molecule
minimum-energy path or PES scan showing accessible radiationless decay in solution
aggregate, crystal, host, or steric constraint blocks access to the crossing geometry
comparison between emissive and non-emissive analogues explained by different CI accessibility
time-resolved or lifetime data supporting fast internal conversion in one state and suppressed decay in another
quantum-chemical evidence such as CASSCF, CASPT2, ADC, TD-DFT, or nonadiabatic dynamics linked to molecule-specific photophysics
explicit negative evidence excluding simpler RIM, TICT, ESIPT, excimer, or packing-only explanations
state/environment-dependent evidence where solution and solid/aggregate have different nonradiative pathways
insufficient_evidence: only mentions internal conversion generically without a molecule-specific crossing pathway
only reports AIE/AIEE phenomenology with no excited-state calculation or decay-path evidence
only uses conical intersection as background theory
only has TD-DFT vertical excitations or orbitals without PES or pathway analysis
evidence is only series-level and cannot be tied to a single candidate molecule
only application or sensing performance without mechanism diagnosis

triage_policy.high: Original research or primary computational mechanism paper with concrete molecule labels, excited-state pathway evidence, and explicit discussion of conical-intersection/radiationless-decay accessibility.
triage_policy.medium: Likely primary source with AIE or state-dependent emission and plausible nonradiative decay/PES evidence, but snippets do not fully show molecule-level CI evidence.
triage_policy.low: Insufficient snippet evidence for automatic inclusion.
triage_policy.reject: Review, patent, tutorial, generic theory page, database-only result, or paper with no clear molecule-level excited-state mechanism evidence.
